elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement without consent to an Affiliate.
elements.evidence: Section 15.6 permits either Party, including PB as Customer, to assign the Agreement and all rights and obligations to any Affiliate without the other Party's consent.

elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement without consent to a successor in a merger.
elements.evidence: Section 15.6 permits either Party to assign to a successor in connection with a transfer of all or substantially all relevant business or assets, expressly including by merger.

elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement without consent to a successor in an acquisition.
elements.evidence: The successor exception covers transfers by merger, sale of stock, sale of assets or otherwise, encompassing an acquisition of PB or the relevant business.

elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement without consent to a successor in a sale of substantially all assets.
elements.evidence: Section 15.6 expressly permits assignment to a successor in connection with a sale or transfer of all or substantially all business or assets to which the Agreement relates.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign the Agreement without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: Section 15.6 allows SFJ as Vendor to assign without PB's consent to any Affiliate or qualifying successor.

elements.element: Customer's consent to a Vendor assignment may not be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: No reasonableness limitation applies to PB's consent. For the specified pre-Program Transfer restriction, the clause expressly allows PB to withhold consent in its sole discretion.

elements.element: Vendor may never assign the Agreement to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: The restriction only addresses entities whose primary business is pharmaceutical or biotechnology development or commercialization, applies only before Program Transfer, and permits transfer with PB's consent. It is not an absolute, perpetual prohibition on assignment to a Customer competitor.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate the Agreement upon Customer's Change of Control.
elements.evidence: Revised Section 14.2.6 expressly states that a Change of Control of PB gives SFJ no right to terminate the Agreement.

elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement without consent to a successor.
elements.evidence: Section 15.6 permits PB to assign the Agreement without consent to a successor in connection with a qualifying merger, stock sale, asset sale or other transfer.

elements.element: Customer must give Vendor written notice of a successor assignment.
elements.evidence: Section 15.6 imposes no notice obligation for successor assignments. Section 14.2.6 requires notice of PB entering into a definitive Change of Control agreement, which is not an assignment-notice requirement and does not demonstrably cover every successor assignment.

elements.element: Vendor may assign the Agreement without consent to a successor.
elements.evidence: The successor exception in Section 15.6 applies mutually and therefore permits SFJ to assign without PB's consent to a qualifying successor.

elements.element: Vendor must give Customer written notice of a successor assignment.
elements.evidence: Neither Section 15.6 nor revised Section 14.2.6 requires SFJ to provide PB written notice of a successor assignment.

elements.element: Customer must obtain Vendor consent for any assignment other than a successor assignment.
elements.evidence: Although consent is generally required, Section 15.6 separately allows PB to assign to any Affiliate without SFJ's consent, even where the Affiliate is not a successor.

elements.element: Vendor's consent to other Customer assignments may not be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: The general consent requirement contains no language preventing SFJ from unreasonably withholding consent.

elements.element: Vendor must obtain Customer consent for any assignment other than a successor assignment.
elements.evidence: Section 15.6 allows SFJ to assign to any Affiliate without PB's consent, even where the Affiliate is not a successor.

elements.element: Customer's consent to other Vendor assignments may not be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: No generally applicable reasonableness standard limits PB's consent, and the special pre-Program Transfer restriction expressly provides for PB's sole discretion.

result.reason: Assuming PB is Customer and SFJ is Vendor, the redline successfully removes SFJ's Change-of-Control termination right and preserves PB's affiliate and successor assignment rights. It does not revise Section 15.6 to impose the preferred Vendor consent and competitor restrictions or the fallback notice and reasonable-consent framework. It is not minimal to attainment of either complete position because neither level is achieved and the redline additionally prohibits suspension and repricing beyond the preferred no-termination requirement. Related termination-payment provisions were appropriately removed, and no clear contradiction with the supplied operative language is introduced. Drafting quality is reduced by the incomplete sentence ending in 'and' in Section 15.6.
